decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up right-arm approach toward the key; key yaw and location differ from the reference.
Continue smooth elbow-up approach, bending wrist downward while moving toward the key.
Move over the key and progressively match its diagonal yaw; maintain elbow-up continuity.
Approach the key shaft with open fingers, slowing as the wrist becomes downward facing.
Center the right fingers over the shaft and remove the remaining key-yaw mismatch before grasping.
Use the wrist image to shift the shaft toward the finger centerline and refine yaw, with gradual preclosure.
Finish centering near the key neck and close the right gripper; retention still requires a lift check.
Lift the closed right gripper by six centimeters and check that the key follows rather than remaining on the table.
The key follows the lifted gripper. Raise and rotate it toward a centerline handover while keeping the right grip closed.
Continue key rotation and lift; start a small, continuous elbow-up motion of the receiving left arm.
Raise the retained key to handover height and continue rotating its bow toward the receiving left gripper.
Move the left hand inward along an elbow-up arc while the right hand rotates the retained key toward the handover pose.
Bring the receiving hand toward the exposed key bow, keeping the arms on their respective sides and the right grip closed.
Align the left gripper horizontally with the bow at a short stand-off; use wrist views to refine handover height.
Advance the left fingers toward the bow and lower them to correct the wrist-view height offset; right hand remains closed.
Refine the left-hand height and advance the last small gap toward the exposed bow before closing.
Close the left fingers on the bow with a small downward centering correction; preserve the right grasp during transfer.
The bow is between the left fingers. Open the right gripper gradually while holding the left pose to test handover retention.
The key slipped free during transfer. Clear the left fingers and lower the open right hand to reacquire it after settling.
Track the dropped key in the right wrist view, translating toward it while leaving the left arm clear.
Lower the right fingers over the settled key neck, using the head and wrist views rather than assuming the dropped key stayed in place.
Align the right fingers with the settled shaft and close at the neck with a small final descent.
Reopen and correct the observed yaw error in the opposite direction, centering the neck before another closure.
The key neck is now centered. Close the right fingers with a small yaw refinement and shallow descent.
Lift the reacquired key with the right gripper closed and verify that it remains between the fingers.
The key follows the right hand. Raise it to the receiving-hand height and return the bow toward the center for a more carefully centered transfer.
Bring the left fingers closer to the bow, correcting its below-center wrist-image position while preserving the right grasp.
Correct the bow's slight high-side offset and insert it farther between the left finger pads before closing.
Seat the bow slightly deeper between the left pads, finish centering, and close the left gripper while the right still supports the key.
With the bow centered between the left pads, release the supporting right fingers gradually and check visual retention.
Withdraw the open right hand to confirm that the left fingers independently retain the key before reorienting it.
The left hand retains the key. Begin its upright reorientation while moving the open right arm safely outward.
Continue the smooth upright reorientation with the retained key, preserving elbow-up continuity and clearing the right arm.
Carry the key toward a hover above the observed lock while continuing its downward orientation; move the right arm toward a clear resting pose.
Continue orienting the retained key upright above the lock; hold the cleared right arm stationary.
Complete the upright hover orientation; inspect the key tip and slot together before any insertion descent.
Use the wrist-view tip-to-slot offset for a small lateral correction and shallow approach, without turning yet.
Back off from the slot and adjust the key's blade-plane yaw; the visible teeth suggest the transferred pose is not yet aligned for insertion.
Tilt about the retained bow at clearance to compensate the off-axis handover grasp; avoid descending until the shaft is upright.
Continue compensating the sideways bow grasp about a fixed pivot, keeping the key clear of the lock.
Continue the bow-centered tilt toward a vertical shaft, preserving clearance and checking retention.
Tilt the held key closer to vertical with a fixed bow position; use small increments to preserve the arm configuration.
Finish most of the upright tilt while raising the bow pivot slightly for clearance and extension margin.
Replan after the continuity rejection: pause translation and correct shaft roll in smaller increments before further tilt.

Continue the small yaw adjustment about the held bow while maintaining insertion clearance and configuration continuity.

Continue the continuous alternate rotation toward slot alignment, holding the key above the lock.
Continue the alternate alignment rotation with only a shallow descent while the key remains visibly above the slot.
